Provider API keys

separate credentials, unchanged default

Store keys for several providers. Credentials are write-only; status describes local declarations, not a successful paid request.

Default provider: anthropicChange it separately in Configuration

  • Anthropic / Claude APIDefaultSet in deployment
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

    Present in the deployment's .env. Presence does not verify that a key works.

An operator can add or replace provider keys.

Find or create a key at the provider

Find or create an API key for Anthropic / Claude API
Get API key at Anthropic / Claude APIOfficial guide
  1. Sign in to Claude Console and open API keys.
  2. Create a key for the intended workspace or service account and copy it when shown.
  3. Paste the new API key into the write-only field here, then preview and confirm.

Claude subscription sign-in and Claude Code setup-token are separate from an Anthropic API key.

Find or create an API key for OpenAI API
Get API key at OpenAI APIOfficial guide
  1. Sign in to OpenAI Platform and select the intended project.
  2. Create an API key and copy it when shown.
  3. Paste the new API key here, then preview and confirm. ChatGPT plan sign-in uses the separate host connection guide.

An API key and Sign in with ChatGPT use different credential and billing routes.

Find or create an API key for Google Gemini API
Get API key at Google Gemini APIOfficial guide
  1. Sign in to Google AI Studio and open API keys.
  2. Choose the intended Cloud project and create or copy a Gemini API key.
  3. Paste it here, then preview and confirm. Vertex credentials use a separate host setup.

Use the Gemini API key flow, not a Vertex or Google account login token.

Find or create an API key for OpenRouter
Get API key at OpenRouterOfficial guide
  1. Sign in to OpenRouter and open Keys.
  2. Create a named key and choose its credit limit.
  3. Copy the key into this write-only field, then preview and confirm.

Saving a key does not select this provider, validate a credential or change model routing.

Find or create an API key for DeepSeek
Get API key at DeepSeekOfficial guide
  1. Sign in to the DeepSeek API platform.
  2. Open API keys and create a key for this deployment.
  3. Copy it here, then preview and confirm.

Saving a key does not select this provider, validate a credential or change model routing.

Subscription authentication

host-owned credentials, safe status only

Subscription credentials stay on the owning host. Use its supported sign-in flow, separately from API keys.

Sign in with ChatGPT on the owning host
Host connection guideOfficial provider guidance
  1. Configure an openai-chatgpt connection and explicit openai binding in the reviewed policy.
  2. On its owning host, run the login command from this deployment with the worker's settings and Valkey context.
  3. Complete the provider browser authorization. A remote browser needs callback port 1455 forwarded to that host.

The console never receives OAuth credentials. Complete the loopback authorization on the owning host; this page does not perform a sign-in.

Claude subscription and community compatibility
Host connection guideOfficial provider guidance
  1. Read the vendor's current authentication restrictions before selecting a community route.
  2. The reviewed pi community adapters are pinned compatibility paths with their own host staging and login instructions.
  3. Official claude setup-token is for Claude Code; its token is not an API key to paste here.

Compatibility with pinned community packages is not vendor endorsement. Follow the host guide rather than pasting a Claude login token.

Subscription status not published

No credential or quota inference can be made from missing host observations.

Notifications

  • Forge comments: on; trigger 3 also keeps a status comment up to date.
  • Failure hook: PI_ON_FAILURE → .../notify, once per paid failure.

The hook's runs are in the worker's log; hook history is not published. Hook rules
